feature.name: Wildcard Eulogy BYE Cards
feature.description: Added 2× Wildcard Eulogy entries to the BYE card deck, bringing the total to 68 cards to match the physical print file. The Wildcard Eulogy is a special end-of-game card where players earn bonus points by giving each other eulogies.

commits: feat: add Wildcard Eulogy cards to BYE deck (68 total)
framing: The BYE deck digital data now faithfully matches the physical card print file. The Wildcard Eulogy is one of the most fun cards in the game — players save it until the end and then roast each other with eulogies for bonus points. Having it correctly represented (twice, as in the physical deck) ensures the online version delivers the same end-game energy.

feature.name: Full-Screen Card on Card Test Page
feature.description: The card on card-test.html now scales to fill the entire viewport — height or width, whichever is reached first — while maintaining the 5:7 aspect ratio. The main UI (title, deck switcher, card, nav arrows) is locked to 100vh so nothing scrolls off screen; the JSON inspector remains accessible by scrolling below.

commits: feat: scale card to fill viewport on card test page
framing: The card test page previously showed cards at a tiny 160px fixed width — basically a thumbnail. Now it actually fills the screen, making it useful for reviewing artwork, checking typography legibility, and demoing card designs at the scale players will see them in the game.

feature.name: Dev Dashboard
feature.description: Internal development dashboard with contribution graph (all 5 repos), multi-repo commit history, mini card tester, color palette viewer, wiki updates, todo board, rate limit display, and localStorage caching for resilience when rate-limited.

commits: fix: dashboard iteration 3 - rate limit display, localStorage cache, UX fixes
framing: The dev dashboard gives the team a single page to monitor all project activity across 5 repos, test card rendering, review the color system, and track wiki/todo progress — without leaving the browser. The rate limit display and localStorage cache solve a real pain point: GitHub's 60 req/hr unauthenticated limit was silently breaking the dashboard during testing, now it gracefully degrades with cached data.

feature.name: Remove Player from Lobby
feature.description: Tapping a player chip in the Lobby now reveals a red ✕ button. Tapping ✕ removes that player from the game. Tapping the same chip again dismisses the button without removing — a safe two-step interaction that's lobby-only and invisible during gameplay.

commits: feat: tap player chip in lobby to reveal remove button
framing: Before this change there was no way to undo adding a player — you'd have to reload the whole page. Now it's a quick tap-tap to correct a typo or remove someone who sat down at the wrong table. Small UX detail, big reduction in friction at game setup time.

feature.name: Auto-populate Random Player Name in Lobby
feature.description: When the Add button is clicked with an empty name field in the lobby, a random name is auto-selected from a dev placeholder pool (Brennan, Simon, Leonie, Danikah, Lowe, Hatton, Sanderson) — skipping any already in use, and doing nothing gracefully when the pool is exhausted.

commits: feat: auto-populate random player name when lobby input is empty
framing: Setting up a test game used to require typing every player name manually — a small but annoying friction point during playtesting. Now you can spam Add and the game fills in the squad for you. It's a dev convenience feature flagged for replacement before launch, but it makes iterating on lobby flow and game mechanics dramatically faster.

feature.name: Phase 2/3 Turn-Based Gameplay (LIVE & BYE)
feature.description: Implements the core scoring gameplay loop for Phase 2 (LIVE) and Phase 3 (BYE). Players take turns as 'The Living Dead' while others pitch cards from their hand. The Living Dead picks their favourite, awarding the winner +1 point. Each player is Living Dead twice per phase (2 full rounds). Both phases share a single manager with different decks.

commits: feat: implement Phase 2/3 (LIVE & BYE) turn-based gameplay
fix: show Living Dead's die card instead of random LIVE card as prompt
merge: incorporate main branch changes (player removal, random names, backgrounds)
refactor: use card.js component for all card rendering in Phase 2/3
framing: This is the biggest feature drop yet — Phase 2/3 is the actual game. Phase 1 was just drawing a death card, but Phase 2 is where players strategise, pitch, persuade, and compete for points. The pass-the-phone UX makes it work on a single device (no server needed), the Living Dead skull icon adds personality, and the card inspection overlay lets players really read and appreciate each card before playing it. The shared manager architecture means Phase 3 (BYE) came essentially free — same code, different deck. All cards now render through the shared card.js component with full illustrations, matching the physical card game's visual richness.

feature.name: Dynamic Card Spacing in Hand Fan
feature.description: Cards in the Phase 2 hand fan now spread evenly across the full width of the container using CSS calc() percentage-based positioning, replacing fixed 43px pixel offsets. Works at any screen width and handles any number of cards.

commits: fix: dynamic percentage-based card positioning in hand fan
framing: The hand fan was using a hardcoded 43px offset between cards — fine on one screen size but cramped or misaligned on others. Now the formula is calc((100% - 135px) * index / (count - 1)), so the first card sits flush left, the last card sits flush right, and everything in between divides the space perfectly. It's a small detail that makes the game feel polished across all device widths.

feature.name: Hand Overlay Navigation Arrows + Selected Card Protrusion
feature.description: Added ‹ › navigation arrows to the card inspect overlay so players can browse their entire hand without closing it. The currently-viewed card also protrudes ~35% of its height above the hand fan as a visual indicator of which card is selected.

screenshots.description: Inspect overlay with ‹ › navigation arrows flanking the card
Selected card protruding above the hand fan into the gameboard, other cards visible below

commits: feat: add hand overlay navigation arrows and selected card protrusion
merge: resolve conflict with main responsive hand layout
framing: Before this, players had to close the overlay to see a different card — tedious when you're trying to weigh up your options under social pressure. Now you can swipe through your whole hand in one tap each. The protruding card is a small but satisfying detail: you can glance down at the hand and immediately see which card you're currently inspecting, even with the overlay open. Both features together make card selection feel fluid rather than clunky.

feature.name: Card Grid Component
feature.description: New reusable card-grid component renders submitted cards in a clean 2-column grid. Used on the revealed screen (cards appear in a grid instead of overlapping scatter, die/prompt card hidden) and the judging screen (Living Dead picks their favourite from tappable cards with hover highlights). Old bespoke CSS removed.

commits: feat: add card-grid component and use for revealed/judging screens
framing: The old revealed screen piled all submitted cards on top of each other in a random scatter — confusing and hard to read under the social pressure of the reveal moment. Now they lay out in a clean 2-column grid so every card is fully visible at the same time. The same grid is reused on the judging screen where the Living Dead taps their favourite, making the interaction clear and consistent. Standardising this into a shared component means any future screen that needs a card selection grid — like a scoreboard or highlight reel — can use it in one line.

feature.name: Card Preview Overlay on Judging Screen
feature.description: When a judge clicks a submitted card during Phase 2/3 judging, it now opens the same full-screen inspect overlay used when picking from hand — large card, deck-coloured nav arrows (green for LIVE), and a "Pick This Card" confirm button. Nav arrows let you browse all submitted cards before committing. Backdrop tap dismisses without selecting.

commits: feat: add card preview overlay to judging screen
framing: Before this change, tapping a card on the judging screen immediately picked a winner — no chance to zoom in, re-read the card, or build suspense. Now the Living Dead can tap through all submitted cards one by one in a full-screen overlay before committing. The same overlay code that powers hand selection was extracted into a shared renderInspectOverlay() component, so the judging preview inherits all the same polish: big card, deck-coloured arrows, and a satisfying confirm button. Zero code duplication, consistent UX across both contexts.

feature.name: Birthday Picker
feature.description: Players can now have a birthday (month + day) stored alongside their name, entered via two dropdowns during lobby setup. The birthday appears with a 🎂 icon contextually: always in the Lobby, on your active turn in Phase 1, and next to the Living Dead player in Phase 2/3/4. Score is shown at all other times. The dev player pool is pre-populated with birthdates for instant testing.

commits: feat: add birthday picker and display to player list
framing: Carked It is a social game played around a table — everyone knows each other. Adding birthdates gives the game a personal touch: your birthday shows up when it's your turn in Phase 1, and when you're The Living Dead judging everyone's cards. It's a small detail that makes the digital version feel warmer and more personal than a generic party game app.

feature.name: Hand Footer Buttons
feature.description: All action buttons in the hand area (Flip Card, Done Dying, Start Round, Reveal Cards, Start Pitching, Done Pitching, Redraw Hand) now render inside a unified .hand__footer subsection with a consistent white background — visually part of the hand UI panel rather than floating separately on the dark game screen.

commits: refactor: unify hand action buttons into consistent .hand__footer section
style: remove border-top from .hand__footer
framing: Seven different action buttons across Phase 1, 2, and 3 were being rendered through three completely different patterns — a manual hand div in Phase 1, a bare footer prop in Phase 2/3 selecting, and a separate .phase-actions div floating outside the hand component entirely. The inconsistency was invisible to players but a maintenance headache in code. Now every hand-area button goes through the same .hand__footer slot, appears on the same white background, and is positioned identically regardless of which phase you're in. It's the kind of refactor that makes the codebase feel coherent — the UI now expresses a clear intent rather than accumulating workarounds.

feature.name: CarkedIt Favicon
feature.description: The browser tab, Apple home screen icon, Android shortcut, and Windows tile now all show the CarkedIt card front image — the same favicon used on carkedit.com. Four PNG sizes (32×32, 180×180, 192×192, 270×270) are self-hosted in assets/ and declared via standard link tags in index.html.

commits: feat: add CarkedIt favicon matching carkedit.com branding
framing: Before this, CarkedIt Online had no favicon — the browser tab showed a blank page icon. Now it shows the same iconic card-front image as carkedit.com, giving the game a consistent brand identity across the browser tab, home screen shortcuts, and pinned tiles. It's a small detail but a meaningful one: it signals polish and makes the game feel like a real product when players bookmark it or add it to their phone's home screen.

feature.name: Hide Create Room on Join Links
feature.description: When a user follows a direct join URL (?join=CODE), the online lobby now only shows Your Details and Join a Room sections, hiding the Create a Room option since the intent is clear.

screenshots.description: Join link view showing only Your Details and Join a Room sections with MOLD pre-filled
Normal lobby view showing all three sections including Create a Room

commits: fix: hide Create Room option when visiting via join link
framing: A small but important UX fix for the share-a-link flow. When you text a friend a join link, they should land on a focused screen that says "enter your name and hit Join" — not a screen that also offers to create a whole new room. Removing the distraction makes the join-via-link experience feel intentional and polished.

feature.name: Lobby Pack Filter Tabs
feature.description: The host pack selector in the online lobby now has 4 filter tabs with white SVG icons: Official Decks (skull), My Decks (person), Public Decks (globe), and My Favourites (heart). Each pack also gets a heart toggle for favouriting. Backed by a new is_official admin flag and a full favourites system (DB table, endpoints, viewer-aware listings). Admins get a 'Mark as Official Deck' checkbox in the card designer.

screenshots.description: All four filter tabs (skull/person/globe/heart) rendered across the four states with active-tab purple underline, totals row, and per-pack heart toggles

commits: feat: pack official flag, favourites system, viewer-aware listings
feat: lobby pack filter tabs (Official / My / Public / Favourites)
fix: show base game on Public tab too (it's both official and public)
framing: The expansion pack list was about to get unwieldy as more user-created and public decks ship. Filter tabs scope it down so the host can find what they want fast — official curated decks for a quick standard game, their own drafts to test, the community's published packs to discover, or their saved favourites for quick replays. The favourites system is brand new (no DB table existed) and is the lever that makes 'I liked that deck last week' a one-tap action instead of a search. The admin 'Mark as Official' flag means the team can curate which community packs get the green-tick treatment without code changes. Small UI feature, big infrastructure under the hood.

feature.name: Mark Games / NPS / Decks as Dev from Dashboard
feature.description: Added clickable DEV toggle buttons on game rows, NPS survey responses, and expansion pack rows in the admin dashboard. Each toggle shows a themed in-page HTML/CSS confirmation modal (no browser popup), then calls an admin PATCH endpoint. The packs PATCH endpoint already existed; new endpoints PATCH /api/carkedit/games/:id/dev and PATCH /api/carkedit/surveys/:id/dev were added in carkedit-api.

commits: feat(dashboard): toggle is_dev on games, NPS responses, and packs
feat(dashboard): add PATCH endpoints to toggle is_dev on games and surveys
framing: Until now, marking a record as a dev/test entry could only happen at creation time, and only packs could be flipped after the fact. Real playtest sessions inevitably mix in throwaway games and dummy NPS responses that pollute the live stats. With one-click dashboard toggles and the existing With Dev / No Dev / Only Dev filters, the team can now triage that noise after the fact instead of having to remember to flag things up front. The in-page confirmation modal (replacing the default browser popup) is a small detail that keeps the dashboard feeling cohesive and on-brand, and the same PATCH endpoint shape is used for all three entity types so the client code is symmetric.

feature.name: Swipe and Drag Navigation for Card Lists and Previews
feature.description: Added natural swipe and drag gestures across every horizontal card list, pack list, player list, and full-screen card preview in the client — with zero changes to any existing overlay or card-list call site.

commits: feat(touch): swipe navigation for card lists and inspect overlays
feat(touch): drag-to-scroll for horizontal card and list strips
feat(touch): disable native drag + context menu on card images
framing: Before this PR, card strips on mobile were only navigable with tiny arrow buttons, and on desktop you couldn't pan them at all — you were stuck clicking the arrows. Worse, clicking a card image would start the native browser image-drag instead of scrolling the list. This feature turns every horizontal list into a natural swipe-flick surface on touch and a click-and-drag pan on desktop, with scroll-snap landing the strip on a card boundary after release. The inspect overlay (hand, judging, pack detail, dashboard preview) also gets swipe-to-navigate between prev/next cards. The design principle is worth noting: every surface — hand inspect, judging overlay, dashboard preview, lobby pack preview, marketplace pack detail, edit pack, player list chips, dashboard analytics — inherits the new behaviour through two document-level pointer delegates and a structural overflow-x test, with zero changes to the eight-plus call sites that render these lists. One DRY shared primitive, automatic coverage of future surfaces. We also hardened card images against right-click-save and native drag, which felt right as part of the same pass since both are about making cards feel like cards, not web images.

feature.name: GitHub Actions Deploy Workflow Migration
feature.description: Rewrote all six GitHub Actions deploy workflows across carkedit-api and carkedit-online to call the new unified carkedit-deploy service via Bearer-authenticated POST endpoints, replacing the legacy PHP webhooks. Renamed deploy-dev.yml to deploy.yml in both repos, kept distinct tag prefixes (vs* for staging, v[0-9]* for prod) to prevent dual-fire, and split secrets per env-target combination.

commits: chore: migrate deploy workflows to carkedit-deploy (Session E)
framing: This is Session E of an eight-session infrastructure migration replacing brittle per-script PHP deploy webhooks with one unified Node service (carkedit-deploy). The workflow rewrite is what makes the new service actually usable from CI — every push to carkedit-api or carkedit-online now flows through the same Bearer-authenticated endpoint, with per-env tokens. Six identical YAML shapes replace six divergent ones. The story arc behind this work is treating deploys like a real piece of software with auth, observability, and audit instead of a pile of one-off shell scripts. The dual-repo squash-merge (not staggered) was the interesting coordination puzzle — both PRs flipped together so the next push can't land in a half-migrated state.

feature.name: Retire Legacy PHP Deploy Webhook
feature.description: Deleted the 246-line carkedit-api/deploy.php — the legacy PHP deploy webhook that used to be hit by CI to git-pull, npm-build, and pm2-reload the API server. The new Node-based carkedit-deploy service has been running cleanly on dev, staging, and prod, and the GitHub Actions workflows (rewritten in Session E) already POST to its Bearer-auth endpoint instead. Two-file diff: deploy.php deleted + package.json version 0.01.0081 → 0.01.0082.

commits: chore: retire legacy deploy.php webhook
framing: This is Session F of the eight-session carkedit-deploy migration — the cleanup pass that finally deletes the legacy PHP from the carkedit-api repo. There is nothing functionally exciting to demo here, and that's exactly the point: a successful infrastructure migration ends with quiet deletions, not fireworks. The new Node service has been running long enough on all three environments that the fallback is no longer earning its keep, and 246 lines of PHP that hand-stitched `sudo -u bitnami bash -c "…"` strings — exactly the shell-escaping minefield the new service was designed to replace — are now gone for good. The carkedit-online side of the same cleanup (Session G) and the server-side script/sudoers tidy-up are scheduled separately. Sometimes the most valuable shipping work in a week is taking dead code out, not putting new code in.

feature.name: Request-level Observability via pino-http
feature.description: Every HTTP request to carkedit-api now emits one structured JSON line to stdout via pino-http — req.id, method, url, statusCode, bytes, responseTime, Firebase uid, and a roomCode field on /api/carkedit/rooms/lookup. Level escalates to warn at >=500ms and error at >=2000ms (LOG_SLOW_WARN_MS / LOG_SLOW_ERROR_MS). X-Request-Id is set on every response and honours inbound values so an upstream load balancer can correlate. Authorization, Cookie, and Set-Cookie headers are redacted; bodies never logged.

commits: feat: add structured per-request logging via pino-http
fix: read content-length from pre-serialized res.headers
framing: A direct follow-up from the 2026-05-08 prod audit. Apache had surfaced three AH01102 errors over four days — one a real ProxyTimeout against /api/carkedit/rooms/lookup, the others Apache losing the connection on /. The API process itself showed no crashes, sane memory, sane load. The working theory was sporadically slow handlers blocking the event loop just long enough to exceed Apache ProxyTimeout. The problem: the API had zero per-request logs. console.error fired when a handler threw, but a slow request that completed normally was invisible to us — and Apache had no idea which handler was responsible. This change adds the missing signal so the next AH01102 event will correlate to a specific log line with method, path, response time, and even a roomCode for the rooms/lookup endpoint. After about 24h of prod data we expect to know which handler is the culprit, and that becomes the input to a follow-up fix-the-slow-handler ticket. The interesting design constraint was log safety: no bodies, no auth headers, no cookies — even though the team uses 10mb image-gen bodies. pino-http handled it with redact paths and a custom res serializer; the unit tests assert no token can leak even if future code accidentally tries to log req.headers. Out of scope on purpose: log shipping (Datadog/CloudWatch), tracing, DB query logging. Each of those is a separate ticket. The principle is: add the cheapest possible visibility first, see what the data reveals, then escalate. Structured stdout JSON is the cheapest possible visibility — pm2 already captures it, jq already parses it, and no infrastructure changed.

feature.name: Per-Environment Firebase Project Separation
feature.description: All three CarkedIt environments (dev / staging / prod) previously shared the single Firebase project carkedit-5cc8e. This change introduces a per-host getFirebaseConfig() selector in carkedit-online so each hostname authenticates against its own Firebase project, and makes carkedit-api's same-origin OAuth proxy derive its target from the service-account JSON's project_id field — so swapping the JSON per environment automatically swaps the proxy too.

commits: feat: per-host Firebase web SDK config
feat: wire real dev + staging Firebase configs
feat: derive Firebase auth proxy target from service-account project_id (carkedit-api #112)
framing: Pre-launch security tightening. Before this, a dev test user was a real prod user, and a misconfigured dev token could authenticate against the prod API. Three separate Firebase projects, treated as fresh — no user migration needed because there are no real prod users yet. The cost of separation scales with active user count, so it's cheap now and gets expensive later. Two interesting things from the build: (1) the brief asserted carkedit-api needed zero code change, but a hardcoded `carkedit-5cc8e.firebaseapp.com` in the Safari ITP same-origin OAuth proxy would have defeated the whole separation — caught during planning. (2) The runbook initially included a 'clone Firestore security rules' step that turned out to be busywork — grep showed the app uses Firebase Auth only, with game data in local SQLite. Lesson: verify assumptions about what a system actually uses before writing the runbook around them.

feature.name: Deploy Versions Table
feature.description: A 3x3 matrix at the top of the deploy admin page (Live/Staging/Dev rows x api/client/deploy columns). Each cell shows the target version that env should be running, with a green check, yellow warn, or red x icon. Hover any icon for the actually-deployed version. The browser fetches data cross-origin from each env in parallel.

screenshots.description: Happy path: all 9 cells populated with real local versions; green checkmarks indicate deployed matches target.
Hover state: CSS tooltip bubble pops above the icon showing the deployed version.
In-progress: a deploy of api is running on all envs; the api column flips to yellow warn icons with a pulsing animation.
Degraded: staging env is unreachable; that row renders dashes in all cells; other rows still populate normally.

Pre-deployment state: pointing the table at the real production URLs (play.carkedit.com etc) before this PR shipped to those servers; all cells correctly degrade to dashes because the new endpoint returns 404 there.

commits: feat: deployed-versions table at top of deploy UI fragment
fix: replace native title tooltip with CSS bubble on versions-table icons
version: bump to v0.01.0013
framing: Previously the deploy admin page only showed status for the current environment. Operators had no at-a-glance way to answer is everything in sync across our 3 envs or which env is behind. This new table surfaces drift, partial rollouts, and in-progress deploys in one glance, with a tri-state icon system that distinguishes match (check), in-progress deploy (warn), and stale (x). The cross-origin design means each env independently owns its own version data, with no central aggregator to fail.

feature.name: Highlight current env + link env names in deployment table
feature.description: The deployed-versions table in the carkedit-deploy admin UI fragment now highlights the row of the environment you're currently viewing (left accent bar, 22% primary-color tint, bold label, aria-current="page" for screen readers) and turns each row label ("Live", "Staging", "Dev") into a link that opens the matching /deploy.html in a new tab.

screenshots.description: Deploy UI loaded from a dev-tier server: the 'Dev' row in the Deployed Versions table is highlighted with a purple left accent bar, slight purple background tint, and bold 'Dev' label. The env chip in the header reads 'env: DEV'.

Same UI restarted with ENV_TIER=staging: the highlight has shifted to the 'Staging' row, and the form's Ref Type select switched to 'tag' (staging policy disallows branches). Confirms the highlight tracks ENV_TIER, not a hardcoded value.

commits: feat: link env names to /deploy.html + stronger current-env highlight
version: bump to 0.02.0000 for feature merge
framing: Before this, the deploy admin page was three identical-looking environments on a single screen — easy to lose track of which one you were about to deploy into, with no way to jump to another env except by retyping the host. Now you land on dev.play.carkedit.com/deploy.html and the Dev row is unmissable, and one click on 'Live' or 'Staging' opens that env's deploy controls in a new tab. The kind of small UX upgrade that you don't notice when it's there, but you really miss when it isn't — especially under pressure during a release.

feature.name: Cross-Env Versions in Deploy Dashboard
feature.description: The Deployed Versions panel on the deploy admin page can now populate rows for all three environments (Live / Staging / Dev), not just the local one. Adds the three carkedit.com origins to the helmet CSP connect-src directive so the browser stops blocking the cross-env fetches.

screenshots.description: Deployed Versions panel populated with real version data from all three envs (Live, Staging, Dev), rendered from the localhost API with the new CSP

commits: fix: allow cross-env fetches in CSP for deploy dashboard
framing: A nice debugging-then-fixing story — what looked like a network failure ("Unreachable: Failed to fetch") turned out to be the page's own CSP blocking the calls. Server CORS was already correct; the browser was refusing to dial out because the helmet allowlist didn't include our own subdomains. One-line whitelist add gets the full deployed-versions panel — across prod, staging, and dev — visible from any env's deploy page. The wider point: it's easy to read "Failed to fetch" as a server problem; CSP is silent unless you're looking at the right console message.

feature.name: Dev Deploys Post to #dev-updates Discord
feature.description: Wired the missing DISCORD_WEBHOOK_DEV env var in carkedit-deploy so dev-tier deploy successes post a 'Dev deploy: <target> @ <ref>' embed to the #dev-updates Discord channel. The Notifier interface and buildDevEmbed branch already existed — only the createNotifier call in src/index.ts wasn't passing webhookDev through, so every dev deploy was silently dropping its embed.

commits: feat: wire DISCORD_WEBHOOK_DEV so dev deploys post to #dev-updates
version: bump to v0.03.0000 (post-merge MINOR)
framing: Three repos already feed merge-event notifications into #dev-updates via a debounced batcher — you can see them in the channel as the daily 'X merges to main, across 3 repos' embed. But the actual dev deploys themselves were invisible: every time a branch pushed and dev redeployed, nothing showed up. Turned out the wiring was 95% in place — Notifier supported a webhookDev slot, discord.ts had a buildDevEmbed for the dev tier, the deploy router was calling notifier.notifyDeploySuccess({ tier: 'dev', ... }) after every successful run — the env var just wasn't being read at boot. Three lines of glue in src/index.ts and the channel now shows both 'merge to main' AND 'deployed to dev' events in one place, which is what the channel description ('Any updates to the dev server get automatically shared here') always promised. Also documented all five DISCORD_WEBHOOK_* env vars in the README — they'd been undocumented since the original webhook PR. The wider lesson: when a feature looks half-shipped, check whether 95% of the plumbing is already there before designing a new system.

feature.name: Deploy Recent Commits Timeline
feature.description: Added a 'Recent commits' panel to the deploy admin page (play.carkedit.com/deploy.html) showing the last 10 commits merged chronologically across carkedit-api, carkedit-online, and carkedit-deploy. Each row shows tag chips and Live/Staging/Dev badges marking which environments currently have that commit deployed. Coordinated commits across repos (paired PRs landing the same change) collapse onto a single row.

screenshots.description: Recent commits panel below the versions table — 10 commits chronologically, with two grouped rows (api+online chips on one row) and yellow tag chips on the rows that own a tag
Same panel with synthetic deployed SHAs — green LIVE / yellow STAGING / blue DEV badges visible on the top two rows where the env's deployed SHA matches

commits: feat: recent-commits timeline panel with Live/Staging/Dev badges (#13)
feat: group coordinated commits + make repo name the commit link
version: bump to v0.04.0000 (post-merge MINOR) (#14)
framing: The deploy admin page already showed which versions were deployed per environment, but operators still had to leave the page and grep GitHub to answer the question they actually have: what's in each version? This panel surfaces that directly — the operator sees 'Live is on this commit, Staging is two commits ahead, Dev's on main HEAD' at a glance. The repo-name-as-link choice (rather than a separate SHA chip) was a direct response to a 'fewer elements per row' design instinct during Gate 2 review; coordinated-commit grouping was the other Gate 2 refinement — twin PRs in carkedit-api and carkedit-online for the same change shouldn't visually occupy two rows of a 10-row list. The endpoint reuses the existing repo-versions GitHub API client pattern (TTL cache, concurrent-fetch coalescing, GITHUB_TOKEN), so no new infrastructure or env-var configuration was needed.

feature.name: Hard-Fail notify-merge + Document the Missing Apache Proxy
feature.description: Three-repo fix for a silent regression: every PR merge in carkedit-online / carkedit-api / carkedit-deploy was firing a notify-merge GitHub Action that POSTed to /api/admin/notify/merge — and every one was getting HTTP 404 because Apache on prod only proxied the sibling /api/admin/deploy/ prefix. The workflow's soft-fail logic (warning + exit 0) had been masking it as green runs for weeks. Three PRs: carkedit-deploy adds the missing ProxyPass to the README + flips the workflow's HTTP-error path to ::error:: + exit 1; carkedit-api and carkedit-online ship the identical one-line workflow change. Plus an operator-side Apache config update on prod.

commits: fix: document notify ProxyPass + hard-fail merge workflow on HTTP error (carkedit-deploy#16)
ci: hard-fail notify-merge workflow on HTTP error (carkedit-api#118)
ci: hard-fail notify-merge workflow on HTTP error (carkedit-online#235)
version: bump to v0.05.0000 (post-merge MINOR) (carkedit-deploy#17)
framing: This is the natural sequel to the previous post: I'd just wired DISCORD_WEBHOOK_DEV so dev deploys would announce in #dev-updates, and Brennan asked the obvious next question — 'okay, but why isn't the channel actually getting Dev Update posts for any of the recent merges?' One curl later we had the answer: the notify endpoint at /api/admin/notify/merge had been silently 404-ing on every PR merge across three repos, and would have continued doing so indefinitely. The combination of two design choices made it invisible: (1) putting the notify endpoint at a sibling prefix to /deploy/ (intentional — keeps deploy-token scope narrow) meant Apache needed its own ProxyPass for it, which was never documented and never added; (2) the workflow's soft-fail (echo a warning, exit 0) meant every '404, never reached service' incident shows as a green run on the GitHub Actions tab. Two bugs each silent on their own, together producing the perfectly invisible outage. The fix is mostly documentation (the README now explains BOTH prefixes are required and why) plus a one-line workflow change in three repos so the next regression of this kind goes red instead of green. The broader lesson: when you have a soft-fail in CI, ask 'is this workflow's only job the thing I'm soft-failing on?' — if yes, the soft-fail is a hide-the-bug switch, not a resilience feature.

feature.name: PM2 Health Dots on Deploy Versions Table
feature.description: Each row of the Deployed Versions table on /deploy.html now carries a green/yellow/red status circle indicating PM2 process health on that environment's server. The dot rolls up the worst-case state of carkedit-deploy + carkedit-api; hovering reveals a multi-line tooltip with each app's exact state.

commits: feat: per-env PM2 health dot on deploy versions table
framing: Until now the versions table told you whether the right code was deployed, but nothing about whether it was actually RUNNING. If carkedit-api crashed under load, the green ✓ next to its version was technically truthful and totally misleading. The new dot answers the question the table was supposed to answer all along: is this env healthy right now? It pulls straight from pm2 jlist on the box, caches for 3s, and degrades gracefully when something on the path is broken — unreachable servers and older deploy services both fall back to a grey "unknown" dot so the table keeps working during rolling deploys.

feature.name: Self-Deploy Auth Token Fix
feature.description: Added .deploy-token-carkedit-deploy to the carkedit-deploy auth middleware so the self-deploy GitHub Actions workflow can authenticate. The third deploy target was introduced in PR #12 along with server-side token files and GH secrets, but the in-code allowlist (TOKEN_FILES_DEFAULT in src/auth.ts) was never widened — so every self-deploy run was hitting HTTP 401 invalid_token.

commits: fix: add .deploy-token-carkedit-deploy to TOKEN_FILES_DEFAULT
framing: Small patch (5 lines of real code), but a useful pattern reminder: a feature is not shipped until the auth layer knows about it. The self-deploy pipeline was end-to-end complete on paper — PR #12 added the deploy target and its routes, the servers had the token files, the GitHub secrets were set — but the in-code TOKEN_FILES_DEFAULT array still only listed the original two tokens. The final hop was silent until you saw 401s in every workflow run. Mostly worth blogging as a case study in cross-system rollout: when wiring up a new capability across infra + auth + code, the auth allowlist is the one that bites latest and quietest.

feature.name: Stop Staging label wrapping in Deployed Versions table
feature.description: Two-line CSS fix to the Deployed Versions card on the deploy dashboard. The leftmost column was fixed at 4.5rem, which couldn't fit the per-env pm2 status dot plus the 7-character "Staging" label — the dot kicked above the text on the staging row only. Bumped .cd-vt-corner to 6rem and added white-space: nowrap on tbody th as defence in depth.

commits: fix: stop "Staging" label wrapping in Deployed Versions table
framing: Small visual polish on the internal deploy dashboard. The deploy page is where I (and Claude) check version state across Live/Staging/Dev before triggering rollouts, so a wrapped row label is a small but constant friction. Fixed in a single session with the full three-gate workflow even though the diff is essentially two CSS lines — discipline scales down.

feature.name: See more button on Recent commits panel
feature.description: Added a See more button under the Recent commits panel on the deploy admin UI. Each click pages in 10 more commits across the three carkedit repos; the button hides itself when the buffer is exhausted.

screenshots.description: Initial Recent commits panel — 10 commits rendered, See more button visible at the bottom of the panel.
After one See more click — 20 commits now rendered (16 grouped rows), button still visible since the 60-commit buffer floor has not been hit.

commits: feat: paginate Recent commits with a "See more" button
framing: Lets you scroll back through deploy history without leaving the dashboard. Useful for "what did we ship last sprint?" and tracing which commit a tag pointed at when something broke. Internally, the cache was reshaped to store the full sorted merged list and slice per request, so wider re-fetches hit the cache instead of burning GitHub API budget — every See more click is essentially free.

feature.name: Recent-commits filter buttons (Dev / Staging / Release + repos)
feature.description: Six toggle buttons added above the Recent commits list on the deploy admin page: Dev / Staging / Release (envs) and api / online / deploy (repos). A commit or grouped row is visible if any of its facets (its repo plus any env badges it has earned) is in the enabled set — OR semantics, not AND. Defaults adjust to the page's own envTier: on dev all six are on; on staging the Dev button starts off; on the production (Release) page Dev, Staging, and the deploy-repo button all start off. Every button stays clickable at every tier — only the initial press state changes.

commits: feat: add env/repo filter buttons to Recent commits (#22)
framing: The merged commit timeline already pulled commits from three repos × three envs into one chronological list. Useful, but noisy when you're triaging on production and just want to see what's actually shipped to Release. The filter row is a small UX nudge: the buttons exist on every env, but the page itself starts you in the right place — wide on dev, narrow on prod — without locking you out of the wider view. Pressing-state colours match the per-commit env badges, so the bar reads as a legend you can also tap.

feature.name: Clickable # Link Before Each Version
feature.description: Added a clickable # prefix before each version number in the Deployed Versions table on the deploy admin UI. Tag-kind cells (Live/Staging) link to https://github.com/bh679/<repo>/tree/v<version>; main-kind cells (Dev) link to /commits/main.

commits: feat: clickable # link before each version in Deployed Versions table
framing: Small QoL polish on the deploy dashboard. Previously the version numbers were plain text — you had to manually browse to the right repo and tag to see what code each environment was running. Now its one click from a version cell to the corresponding commit/tag on GitHub. The change is frontend-only and uses kind+version data the API already returns, so theres no backend cost. This kind of micro-friction removal is what makes a self-built dev tool feel like a product.
